communication_obligations: S16: state that no compensation is payable because the recorded cause is WEATHER, which is an extraordinary circumstance under S3.2 -- not because of the length of the delay. Duty of care under S4 is owed anyway (S4.3).

S3.1: the passenger's account of the cause ("Crew did not turn up / crew shortage (as told by gate staff).") differs from the operational record (WEATHER). Say so plainly. Do not ignore the discrepancy and do not adopt their account to avoid an awkward conversation. The record is authoritative and a representative never amends a cause code (S16).
S4.3: describe duty of care as an entitlement. It is never goodwill and never offered instead of compensation.
Our record shows AK808 on 3 Aug was cancelled due to WEATHER (freezing fog at Edinburgh), which is classed as an extraordinary circumstance under policy S3.2.

Because the recorded cause is extraordinary, statutory compensation is not payable (S5.1(b)). Arrival delay at the final destination is not established in the record because no re-routing was completed; the compensation outcome here rests on cause (S16, S5).
Duty of care is owed regardless of cause (S4.3). Your hotel expense will be reimbursed against receipt within the cap of £180 per room per night for up to 3 nights (S4.2, S4.4).

If you also had meals/refreshments or surface transport costs due to the cancellation, these are reimbursable against receipts within the caps of £30 per passenger per 6 hours (meals) and £45 per journey (transport) (S4.2).

If you have specific written evidence that the cause was crew-related (for example a written statement or recorded airport announcement), please provide it and we will refer the cause for review by our Operations Liaison team (S3.1).
On cancellation you may choose either a re-routing to Amsterdam or a full refund of the unused ticket — the choice is yours (S6.1, S7.1). Please let us know your preference.
